paragraphs.text: # ployenv
**English** | 简体中文

A portable, single-binary version manager for local runtimes —
**Node.js, Java, Go, Python, Maven, a

db (Android platform-tools) and Rust** —
with nothing to install and nothing to configure.

No installer, no account, no licence checks, and **no changes to your system
environment**. Drop one

executable anywhere; its runtimes and settings live next
to it.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why ployenv

- **Non-invasive** — never edits the system `PATH`, `.npmrc`, `pip.ini` or the
registry. Activating

a version affects one terminal window only.
- **Explicit** — official sources by default. ployenv ad

opts an existing
installation only when you ask it to, and never guesses.
- **Predictable** — the ef

fective version comes from a project file (`.ployenv`,
plus `.nvmrc`, `.tool-versions` and friends)

or from one global default, and
`PLOYENV_<LANG>_VERSION` overrides both. Nothing ever falls back to

"some
installed version".
- **Portable** — a single ~7.5 MB static binary with zero third-party
depe

ndencies. Move the folder, keep everything.
- **Scriptable** — `--json` output is pure ASCII (non-AS

CII characters are
escaped as `\uXXXX`), so it survives any console code page.
## Install

Windows 10/11 is the primary target; Linux and macOS (amd64/arm64) are built and
validated on native

runners by CI. The macOS binaries are unsigned and unnotarized,
so the first run may need `xattr -d
com.apple.quarantine`. Building needs **Go 1.22+**.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Or, if script execution is allowed:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then put the binary on your `PATH`, for example `D:\PloyEnv\ployenv.exe`.
## Quick start
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Pin a project by adding a `.ployenv` file next to its source:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`ployenv use node@20 --project` writes or updates this file for you.
## Documentation

The full command reference, configuration and troubleshooting guide lives in
**docs/manual.md** (简体中

full command reference, configuration and troubleshooting guide lives in
**docs/manual.md** (简体中文).
Highlights:
| Command | Description |

| `ployenv support` | List supported runtimes |
| `ployenv available <lang>` | Installable versions

|
| `ployenv doctor` | Paths, writability and resolution report |
| `ployenv config` | Show or chang

or` | Paths, writability and resolution report |
| `ployenv config` | Show or change every setting |
Run `ployenv --help` for the built-in summary.
## Roadmap
**Done**

- [x] Portable data directory, one-time base configuration
- [x] Node.js, Java, Go, Python and Maven

, each described by a built-in Spec
- [x] Mirror fallback, and interrupt-safe cleanup (`Ctrl+C` leav

es no partial files)
- [x] Checksum verification where upstream publishes one: SHA-256 for Go archiv

es,
SHA-512 for Maven (node / Java / Python checksums still to come)
- [x] Session activation withou

t touching the system environment
- [x] `--json` machine interface
- [x] Prebuilt archives published

to GitHub Releases (windows / linux / darwin on
amd64 / arm64, with checksums)
**Next**

- [ ] Configurable runtime definitions (FR-11). Today runtime definitions are
compiled-in Go code; `

config.json` cannot add or override one yet
- [ ] Checksums for node, Java and Python, and a `doctor

` connectivity check
against every configured download source
- [ ] Remaining runtimes on the same `

Spec` definition, including the database
and middleware kinds (`MySQL`, `Redis`, `Nginx`) that alrea

dy have a
reserved `kind` field
- [ ] shell completion scripts; `--dry-run` is rejected until it is

implemented (it used to be accepted and silently ignored, BUG-020)
- [ ] Log rotation honoring `logs

ented (it used to be accepted and silently ignored, BUG-020)
- [ ] Log rotation honoring `logs.keep`
**Not planned**

- Automatic switching on `cd` — it needs a global shell hook, which would break
the non-invasive pro
mise. Use `ployenv shell` in each project terminal.
